newsitem.title: UK: Labour would delay EMU entry, Cook tells paper.
newsitem.headline: Labour would delay EMU entry, Cook tells paper.

text.p: The opposition Labour Party would delay Britain's entry into European Monetary Union (EMU) if it came into power, but would join eventually, its foreign affairs spokesman said in an interview published on Monday. A Labour government would find it difficult to join a single European currency right off, Robin Cook, foreign affairs spokesman for the party, told the Financial Times newspaper.
"We can only assess the situation in government. But any intelligent person can see that the obstacles are formidable," Cook was quoted as saying.

Labour, widely tipped to win the next election which must be called by May, is generally more pro-Europe than the ruling Conservatives. But political analysts say this has never meant quick membership of a single currency.
EMU is expected to take place in two stages. The first stage would include Germany, France, Austria, Netherlands, Luxembourg and Belgium.

The Conservatives' long-established position is to decide on EMU when they have to, not before. Prime Minister John Major's cabinet has agreed that any decision to join during the next five-year parliament would be put to a referendum.
Recent polls show more than half of British voters were against Britain joining a single currency at the first opportunity in 1999.
